title: Ignatius on the road
hookLine: chained on his way to the lions, he writes that he is God's wheat (Romans 4)

cards: A prisoner is being marched overland toward Rome, chained to a squad of soldiers. He calls them ten leopards, and says they only get worse when they're treated kindly.
He is Ignatius; in his letters he calls himself the bishop of Syria, and tradition places his church in Antioch. He is going to Rome to die in the arena.
Along the road, Christians come out to meet him in the towns he passes, and he writes letters to their churches. One goes ahead of him, to the Christians in Rome, and it's a strange letter.
It's a request: please, don't save me.

teach.b: Ignatius worries that the Roman Christians will try to step in. So he writes, in effect: say nothing on my behalf. Then comes the picture that gives today its line.

I am God's wheat, he writes, and I am ground by the teeth of wild beasts, so that I may be found pure bread of Christ. Wheat isn't finished when it's harvested. It has to be ground before it can feed anyone.

teach.h: EXCEPT A CORN OF WHEAT FALL.
teach.b: Some readers hear an echo of Jesus in John's Gospel: "Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit."
And for Christians who share bread at the Lord's table, the picture of becoming bread is hard to miss. Readers hear this letter in different ways.
Some are moved by a man so sure of Christ that he walks toward the arena without flinching. Some are uneasy, and ask whether he wanted death too much. Both take the letter seriously.
And notice the rest of the road.

A condemned man, with every reason to think only of himself, spends his last journey writing to other people's churches: be united, gather together often, care for the widows, be patient with one another.

teach.h: BREAD FOR OTHERS, LETTER BY LETTER.
teach.b: Letter by letter, he was already becoming bread for people he would never see again.

how: Catholic, Orthodox and Anglican churches remember Ignatius of Antioch as a saint and martyr, and his letters are read today among the writings of the Apostolic Fathers.

games.q: you're a Christian in Rome with friends in high places. Ignatius is being marched to the arena. what do you do?
o: use your friends to get him released.
do what he asks: don't interfere.
games.why: he begs the Romans not to save him: he is God's wheat, to be ground into pure bread of Christ.

practice: Bread is ordinary: it gets broken, shared, eaten, gone.

Bring to mind the people your days feed in some way, the ones you cook for, work for, listen to, look after, and picture each one for a breath, along with what in you is being ground down right now, tiredness, patience, time, that could still feed someone.
If you pray, offer your day to God as bread; if you don't, simply hold the people who depend on you.

wordCard.voice: Ignatius. A bishop chained on the way to Rome, writing to churches as he goes, and asking the Romans to let him become God's wheat.

orig.note: Greek: I am God's wheat (Ignatius, to the Romans 4).

carryVoice: Your line: god's wheat. Ground first, and then shared with others. Day seven hundred fifty-five.
